concepts.def: Three cells per hemisphere redistribute heat from Equator to poles.
Tropical cell from 0 to ~30 degrees latitude, rising near Equator.
Mid-latitude cell from ~30 to ~60 degrees, driven by other cells.
High-latitude cell from ~60 to 90 degrees, sinking cold air at poles.
Rigid slabs of crust and upper mantle moved by mantle convection.

walkthroughs.h2: Heat is uneven across the planet.
walkthroughs.body_html:
Heat is uneven across the planet.

The atmosphere has three cells in each hemisphere that move heat poleward.

Hadley, Ferrel and Polar.

In the Hadley cell, warm air rises at the Equator.

It cools and sinks around 30 degrees, creating arid deserts.

Surface trade winds blow back toward the Equator.

Plates float on the asthenosphere.

At divergent boundaries they pull apart; at convergent ones they collide.

Conservative boundaries slide past, like California's San Andreas.

mcqs.q: Which cell lies between the Equator and ~30 degrees latitude?
options: Polar
Ferrel
Hadley
Walker

mcqs.q: The San Andreas Fault is which type of plate boundary?
options: Convergent
Divergent
Conservative
Collision

mcqs.q: What drives the movement of tectonic plates?
options: Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
The Earth's rotation makes the plates move.
Convection currents in the mantle combined with slab pull at subduction zones and ridge push at constructive boundaries.
Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.

mcqs.q: What happens at a constructive (divergent) plate boundary?
options: At constructive boundaries the plates collide and build mountains.
At constructive boundaries the plates slide past each other sideways.
Plates move apart, magma rises to fill the gap and solidifies, forming new oceanic crust — for example at the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.

mcqs.q: What weather does an anticyclone (high pressure system) bring?
options: Descending air warms and dries, suppressing cloud formation — so anticyclones bring clear, settled weather: hot in summer, cold and frosty in winter.
Anticyclones bring heavy rainfall because they trap moisture.
High pressure brings stormy weather because the air pushes down hard.
At constructive boundaries the plates slide past each other sideways.

Surface winds blow toward the equator in the Hadley cell
Sinking air creates deserts at the tropics
Mid-latitude winds within the Ferrel cell
Cold descending air at the poles
